newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close higher in thinly-traded session.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close higher in thinly-traded session.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended barely higher in a thinly-traded Friday session, dealers said.
The benchmark September contract closed 0.15 cent firmer at 74.95 cents per lb, having ranged from 75.80 to 74.40 cents. The rest of the board finished up 0.10 to 0.65 cent.
An estimated 1,800 lots changed hands on the day compared with Wednesday's official 1,926 lots.
Prices continue in their overall downtrend amid a record Florida crop and slack demand for juice that has been exacerbated by high retail prices.
Adding to the negative tone was the U.S. Department of Agriculture's upward revision of the 1996/97 Florida crop to a record 225.7 million 90-lb boxes, from 224.2 million boxes.
The USDA also raised yields to 1.58 gallons per box from 1.57 gallons.
Analysts expect the benchmark September contract to ease to 70.00 cents in the near term, followed by the 1993 low of 65.45 cents per lb.

"With a huge carryover anticipated and prospects for another bumper harvest it is difficult to get excited about this market, even at historically low levels," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said in a weekly market comment.
The market dismissed news of a Medfly sighting in Florida as the citrus crop has been harvested and the pests are not a major concern for processed juice.
"The Medfly gets a lot more press than it deserves," an analyst said.

Florida agriculture officials set about 2,000 traps in a 4.5 mile (7 km) radius around a sour orange tree north of Orlando, where the Medfly was found. The state will begin aerial spraying with the pesticide malathion, if a single fly is caught.
